_comment: Copy to test_data_config.json and configure for your environment. Use ${ENV_VAR} for secrets — never commit real credentials.
description: Synthetic healthcare data model with Synthea-generated patient records. Supports JDBC (PostgreSQL) and Object Store (S3/MinIO Parquet) sources. One-time environment setup required — populate using a Synthea data generator run before executing tests.

h360_lake.description: Synthea-generated Parquet files in S3/MinIO, Hive-partitioned by entity type

data_injection._comment: Maps API parameter names to datasource queries. Keys match placeholder variable names in *_data.json rows (e.g. '{{patientId}}' in the data file → resolved by query below).

patientId.query: SELECT patient_id FROM clinical.patients WHERE active = true ORDER BY RANDOM() LIMIT 20
patientId.description: Active patient UUIDs — used in /patients/{patientId} and as filter on child resources

encounterId.query: SELECT encounter_id FROM clinical.encounters WHERE status = 'finished' LIMIT 10

orgId.description: Organization IDs — used for multi-tenant filtering and org-scoped endpoints

claimId.query: SELECT claim_id FROM read_parquet('${H360_LAKE_URI}/claims/*.parquet') WHERE status = 'active' LIMIT 10

providerId.description: Provider UUIDs — used in /providers/{providerId} and care team assignments

duckdb_examples._comment: DuckDB is used as the unified query layer for both JDBC and Object Store sources.
duckdb_examples.jdbc_attach: INSTALL jdbc; LOAD jdbc; ATTACH 'jdbc:postgresql://${H360_DB_HOST}:5432/h360' AS h360 (TYPE JDBC); SELECT patient_id FROM h360.clinical.patients WHERE active=true LIMIT 20;
duckdb_examples.cross_source: SELECT p.patient_id, o.org_id FROM h360.clinical.patients p JOIN read_parquet('s3://bucket/orgs/*.parquet') o ON p.org_id = o.org_id WHERE p.active = true LIMIT 10;

environment_setup.description: One-time setup steps before running tests
steps: 1. Generate synthetic data: run Synthea (https://synthea.mitre.org/) with desired population size
2. Load JDBC data: import Synthea CSV output into PostgreSQL h360.clinical schema
3. Load Object Store data: upload Synthea Parquet output to ${H360_LAKE_URI}
4. Verify: run DuckDB examples above to confirm data is accessible
5. Set env vars: H360_DB_HOST, H360_DB_USER, H360_DB_PASSWORD, H360_LAKE_URI, H360_LAKE_ACCESS_KEY, H360_LAKE_SECRET_KEY
